decisions: User decision (Nov 13, answered 'agree' to the agent's proposal): visible non-ASCII characters stay allowed in .ts files (criterion 3). Only invisible and control characters are forbidden raw. The alternative, ASCII only, was rejected as going beyond the rule borrowed from pasokh.

Agent choice, read by the user who then told the agent to continue: the two raw byte order marks already on main (src/gitlog.ts line 99, tests/gitlog.test.ts line 122) are replaced with escapes in this same change (criterion 8), because the new test cannot pass otherwise. Behavior is unchanged.

Agent choice, read by the user who then told the agent to continue: findRawInvisible lives in scripts/source-hygiene.ts (factory tooling), not in src/, because it is not part of the product's API. It has no command line entry and touches no process stream; the test is the enforcement point.

Agent choice: forbidden characters are defined by Unicode general category (Cc except tab and line feed, Cf, Zs except U+0020, Zl, Zp) plus U+FFFD, using the regular expression property escapes of the JavaScript engine, rather than by a hand-written list of code points. A lone surrogate is not reported (criterion 4 says so); a file read with a fatal UTF-8 decoder cannot contain one.

Agent choice: the test walks src/, tests/ and scripts/ from its own location and checks .ts files only. tests/fixtures/ holds raw bytes on purpose (config-bom.json, config-invalid-utf8.json, two .bin logs) and has no .ts file. The test also asserts that the walk found five known files, so an empty walk cannot pass silently.
Agent choice: files are decoded with a fatal UTF-8 decoder and ignoreBOM: true, so a byte order mark at the start of a file is kept in the text and reported like any other.

Agent choice: BACKLOG.md also gains the row T-029 (a Qodo review for the label lane in a separate job, scheduled for Day 16) in this change. It is a planning row requested by the user, not part of T-028's criteria.
